paper.title: Localized-magnon erosion map of the sawtooth chain (detuning axis)

model.name: sawtooth-chain
model.lattice: sawtooth (delta) chain, N sites = N/2 unit cells

method.tool: scipy sparse eigensolver (pf/ed.py), anchors cross-checked with XDiag (scripts/xdiag_crosscheck.jl)

settings.sector: every $S^z$ sector (magnetization curve from zero-field sector energies)

method.note: Exact diagonalization in each magnetization sector. Because $S^z$ is conserved, the field only contributes $-h S^z$, so the full magnetization staircase follows from zero-field sector energies without scanning $h$.

params.name: system size $N$
params.source: we choose — issue asks for the detuning axis at reconnaissance scale
params.why: largest sizes a laptop finishes in seconds; N=12 anchors (Lucas(6)=18) are exact closed forms
params.risk: too small → erosion widths Γ(δ) carry O(1/N) finite-size offsets
params.fix: report both sizes; N=20–28 reserved for cluster (docs/sawtooth-ed-feasibility.md)

params.name: detuning grid $\delta$
params.source: we choose — issue fixes only the $\delta=0$ exact point
params.why: spans the regime where localized-magnon features visibly erode
params.risk: too coarse → miss asymmetric smearing across $\delta=0$

risks: exact anchors hold only at $\delta=0$; detuned points are numerical, not closed-form
candidate Γ(δ) asymmetry is unverified — needs N=20–28 + degenerate-PT cross-check before it is a claim

figures.expected: at $\delta=0$: single jump $\Delta M = M_{sat}/2$ at $h_{sat}=4J_1$ with Lucas-number degeneracy; at $\delta\neq0$: the jump smears into a staircase

results.why: every closed-form anchor of the issue (flat band, jump, Lucas degeneracy, residual entropy, Monti–Sütő) reproduced to 1e-8–1e-10; smearing at δ≠0 as expected

figures.plots: erosion observables $W(\delta)$, $\Delta M(\delta)$, $\Gamma(\delta)$ vs one-magnon bandwidth

observe.quantity: plateau width W, jump size ΔM, smearing width Γ of the magnetization curve

figures.expected: W(δ) shrinks linearly; ΔM drops from M_sat/2 to a smooth rise; Γ(δ) ≈ one-magnon bandwidth if smearing is single-particle physics

results.why: Γ(δ) tracks the one-magnon bandwidth → smearing is single-particle physics; candidate new observation: Γ exceeds bandwidth for δ<0 but not δ>0 (unverified, flagged in risks)
